item.title: Massachusetts neighbours lose appeal over $3.7 million verdict for disrupting couple's home construction
item.description: In the divorce proceedings between Vernon and Nichole McIntosh, the court mandated a substantial division of assets following Vernon's misappropriation of funds. Nichole is awarded 55 percent of the marital estate, amounting to over $138,000. The trial established that Vernon hid and mismanaged marital assets during the divorce. Properties purchased during their marriage will be sold, with net proceeds evenly distributed. Vernon must also cover Nichole's attorney fees.

item.title: Texas appeals court overturns tenant's $250,000 award over defective legal notice to landlord
item.description: A Texas appeals court has overturned a significant $250,000 default judgment that was previously granted to a tenant due to flaws in the service documentation. Lavender Apartments LLC contested the validity of the delivery records, claiming they did not adhere to Texas legal standards. As the court found the required service was inadequately demonstrated, the case will go back for additional litigation and examination in the trial court.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Utah court backs family's claim to disputed farmland after 1965 fence outweighs neighbour's survey
item.description: A Utah family successfully upheld its legal rights to a disputed piece of farmland after a court ruling. The Christiansen Family Trust contested boundary claims made by Haas Land & Livestock, which purchased neighboring property. The property dispute centered around a fence built in 1965 that marked the boundary. The Utah Court of Appeals affirmed earlier decisions favoring the Christiansens' long-accepted boundary.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Ohio residents push data center ban as $5bn Amazon project faces November 10 hearing
item.description: Residents in Butler County are rallying against the proposed Amazon data center, voicing worries over possible water shortages, noise pollution, and pollution from backup generators. Local zoning authorities have suggested prohibiting data centers in St. Clair Township, where this project is slated to occur. A crucial public hearing is set to address these issues alongside zoning matters. Recent trends show rising voter favor for restrictions on similar undertakings across Ohio.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Prince Harry exits BetterUp chief role after 5 years on $1 million salary, takes senior adviser post
item.description: Prince Harry has stepped down as chief impact officer at BetterUp after five years, moving into a senior adviser role at the US-based mental health and coaching company. The Duke of Sussex reportedly earned $1 million annually during his tenure. The development comes weeks after his return to the UK with Meghan Markle and their children, drawing attention to his professional plans.

item.title: US court rejects malpractice claim over lawyer's missed deadline to correct $100,000 divorce debt error
item.description: In a recent ruling, an Arizona appeals court upheld a decision to dismiss a woman's malpractice claim against her ex-attorney. The court concluded she suffered no direct financial loss from the attorney's missed deadline, despite a $200,000 error in the divorce decree regarding familial debt. It was established that the obligation to pay the debt remained unchanged and fully enforceable.

item.title: Kentucky court keeps father 500 feet from home despite sole ownership claim after wife's death
item.description: A Kentucky court has upheld a key decision safeguarding the welfare of two boys by ruling against their father's attempt to rescind protective orders. Although he is the property owner, the court has ordered him to maintain a 500-foot separation from his home. This ruling, following the untimely death of the boys' mother in 2025, emphasizes the priority given to their security over the father's interests.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Big Hill Transmission Line: Kentucky judge blocks EKPC eminent domain bid; appeal moves to higher court
item.description: On April 2, 2026, a pivotal court ruling supported Berea College in its fight over forest land against East Kentucky Power Cooperative. The court's decision underscored that the EKPC's proposal for a transmission line inadequately assessed the environmental attributes of the forest. This ruling emphasized the importance of community involvement in such cases. However, the legal battle is far from over, as EKPC intends to challenge the court's decision.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Matt Damon's Water.org reaches 1 million people in Latin America through Ripple partnership
item.description: Water.org, co-founded by Matt Damon and Gary White, works tirelessly to combat the global water crisis. Through a partnership with Ripple, they have secured innovative financing solutions for families in Latin America. Ripple has committed $6 million to support WaterCredit, enabling affordable loans for water access. This initiative has already empowered over 1 million people with safe water, as they strive to reach 200 million by 2030.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Record Nantucket Estate Sale: 57 Hulbert Avenue fetches $42.5m; $850,000 goes to Land Bank
item.description: A historic waterfront estate in Nantucket Harbour was sold for $42.5 million, breaking the previous record. The property, known as Blue Waters, was owned by the Fife family for over 50 years. The sale took place on November 5, 2026, and generated $850,000 for local land conservation. The estate features direct beach access and a unique architectural design.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Oregon couple in their 70s win over $8 million after firms foreclose on home they still lived in
item.description: An Oregon couple in their 70s have been awarded more than $8 million after a jury found companies liable for unlawfully foreclosing on their home while they were still living in it. The Salem couple had also been denied more than $175,000 left over from the foreclosure sale, which took place in 2022. The jury found that the companies had carried out unlawful trade practices and financially abused the elderly homeowners.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meet Leo Toake, 16, who turned potato peels into weedkiller and restored 15 acres in New Jersey
item.description: At just 16 years old, Leo Toake from New Jersey is on a mission to create a revolutionary herbicide sourced from food scraps. Through his nonprofit, Re:Imagine Inc., he's mobilized over 70 volunteers for habitat restoration and invasive species removal. Early trials of Toake's S.A.F.E. clearly show an 82.5% effectiveness against Japanese stilt grass, all while repurposing over 500 pounds of food waste and contributing to a cleaner environment.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk
